[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really quick agenda 	6 renewal check-in, capacity growth ask, and the multi-region stuff. Mark, do you want to kick off with where you are on timeline?
[00:22] Mark (Nova Health - CTO): Yeah thanks Samira. We're on, um, track to decide by end of month. Primary asks are predictable throughput, lower p99 latency for west coast users, and we need compliance sign-off. So two things: can we do 2x the reserved pool and spin up us-west-2 and eu-west-1?
[00:44] Samira: Totally. We can do that. We'll need to update the reserved capacity quote and also check capacity in those regions. Diego, is that straightforward?
[00:50] Diego (Redwood SE): Yeah in principle. The only caveat is GPU availability per region; we can offer reserved pool with burst capacity. For latency SLOs we'll also suggest continuous batching tweaks and KV-cache prefixing. Note: sometimes our auto-batcher, um, can increase throughput but we tune for p99.
[01:12] Ruth (Nova Health): Quick Q on fallbacks 	6 if a region has a shortage, what's the automatic behavior? We can't have traffic spike cross the ocean for every request.
[01:22] Diego: Good question. We have smart routing by policy 	6 you can route by latency then cost then region. For DR we can route to the nearest region but also have model variants (smaller quantized models) as a fallback to keep latency under SLO. There's also an option to queue short bursts into a prioritized burst pool.
[01:40] Daniel (Security Lead): On security 	6 we need SOC 2 Type II evidence, encryption key management detail (KMS/HSM), audit logs, and SSO integration. Also VPC peering or private link for traffic. Do you have those docs?
[01:55] Priya (Redwood CSM): Yes, we can share SOC 2 and the network topology. We support SAML SSO, RBAC, and customer-managed KMS for Private deployments. For Dedicated we have options for VPC peering and private endpoints, and we maintain audit logs at the route/token level.
[02:14] Mark: Great. Pricing is the other piece 	6 can you put together an amended quote for 2x capacity plus the two regions and the extension term? We're thinking 12 month extension.
[02:26] Samira: Absolutely. We'll send an updated quote. Quick clarifying question: you said 2x reserved. Is that steady-state or peak?
[02:34] Ruth: That's steady-state. We expect baseline traffic will double over next 6 months.
[02:40] Diego: Ok so we'll size for steady-state 2x and configure autoscale policies for bursts. We'll propose a mix of reserved GPUs with a small burst buffer. That keeps units cheaper per token.
[02:52] Mark: Also want to ensure model variants 	6 we use a bigger LLM for patient summarization and a lighter one for routing. Can Redwood host both and have fallbacks?
[03:03] Samira: Yes, you can pin model versions and have automatic fallback to quantized variants. We'll document the recommended quant and batching profiles for your workload.
[03:12] Ruth: On the benchmarking 	6 we'd like a reproducible run. Diego, can you do a 50k tokens/day sim on dedicated pool? We'll check latency and token cost.
[03:22] Diego: Yep, we can provision a temporary dedicated pool and run the sim. Need a 2 hour window for network/firewall changes from your side.
[03:30] Daniel: We can open a window. I'll coordinate with our infra team. Also please send the exact IP ranges and steps.
[03:36] Samira: We'll include that in the doc we send. Priya will include the topology and SOC2 report.
[03:42] Ruth: One small thing 	6 we have data residency concerns for EU users. eu-west-1 must have data retention and KMS keys located in-region. Is that supported?
[03:52] Priya: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS and per-region key scopes for private deployments. For hosted, we can pin to region and enforce residency controls as part of the Dedicated offering. We'll add that to the proposal.
[04:04] Mark: Ok good. Any risks we should be aware of? Latency outliers at p99 are our main worry.
[04:12] Diego: We'll share recommended tokenization and prompt engineering tips to reduce effective sequence length. Also we recommend prefix caching for repeated context to lower token count. There's a small transcription note 	6 sometimes the term KV cache was transcribed as K-V chase in our internal notes 	6 sorry, MC.
[04:29] Samira: (laughs) Noted. We'll make sure docs are clear.
[04:33] Daniel: On compliance again 	6 we might need a security questionnaire for procurement. Can you fill out the standard vendor questionnaire?
[04:40] Priya: Yes please forward it to priya@redwood.example and we'll fill and return. We also can provide a SOC2 letter and penetration test summary.
[04:52] Mark: About the contract term 	6 if we commit to 12 months and 2x reserved, what's the discount? Rough ballpark now is fine.
[05:00] Samira: We'll include tiered pricing in the quote. Ballpark for 2x reserved and longer term is usually 15-25% depending on burst needs and commitment. We'll be explicit in the quote.
[05:12] Ruth: Will there be any migration work to move production to dedicated? We currently run on Redwood Hosted.
[05:19] Diego: Migration is usually straightforward 	6 mostly networking and model pinning. We provide runbooks and a migration checklist. For heavy KV cache usage we recommend warm-up runs. Diego: (almost overlapping) Also we'll run a side-by-side smoke test before cutover.
[05:37] Mark: Ok that sounds good.
[05:40] Samira: Recap of next steps: 1) Samira sends updated quote + draft amendment, 2) Diego schedules benchmark and shares run details, 3) Priya sends SOC2 and network diagram, 4) Daniel confirms network window. Anything else?
[05:55] Daniel: Please include point-of-contact for escalation and SLOs in the amendment. We want clear p99 targets and credits.
[06:03] Priya: We'll add SLA language and the support escalation path.
[06:08] Mark: Great. If the benchmark looks good and the quote is reasonable we can sign the amendment and start roll-out in April.
[06:15] Samira: Fantastic. Thanks everyone. We'll aim to get docs out by Wednesday.
[06:22] Ruth: Thanks.
